## Scientific publishing, open access and research integrity

### IA na redação científica: ética, regras editoriais e boas práticas de reporte {#ia-escrita-cientifica}

*Upcoming · October 2026, annual meeting of the Graduate Programme in Animal Biology, UFMS
(Campo Grande) · and December 2026, UNILA (Foz do Iguaçu) · 40 min · in Portuguese*

Where generative AI stands in the writing of a scientific paper: authorship
and responsibility, the policies of the five largest publishers plus Cambridge
and OUP, Brazil's CNPq Ordinance nº 2.664/2026, COPE's position, the known
limits of LLMs, and the AIdIT framework for reporting AI use. Every quoted
policy comes from the publisher's own page; the deck closes with its own AI
use declaration.

Companion hands-on workshop: [*IA na revisão de literatura*](teaching.qmd#ia-revisao-literatura).

[{{< fa solid display >}} Open the slides](https://provetelab.org/ia-escrita-cientifica/){.btn .btn-outline-primary}
&nbsp;
[{{< fa brands github >}} Source](https://github.com/diogoprov/ia-escrita-cientifica){.btn .btn-outline-secondary}

### FAIR and CARE peer review and publication {#esa-fair}

*11 August 2025 · contribution INS 01-03 to the session “Ecology Is Everywhere,
But It Needs to CARE and Be FAIR” (1:30–3:00 PM EDT, Hilton Key 7) ·
Ecological Society of America Annual Meeting, Baltimore · in English*

Why the publication system around ecological data is slow, opaque and siloed,
and what a FAIR-aligned review and dissemination pipeline would have to look
like instead. From the vantage point of a senior editor at *Journal of
Biogeography* and *Ecology and Evolution*. The deck carries the subtitle
*Fostering a Transparent Publication Ecosystem*.

[{{< fa solid file-pdf >}} Slides (PDF, 19 pp.)](talks/2025-esa-fair-peer-review.pdf){.btn .btn-outline-primary}
&nbsp;
[{{< fa solid calendar-days >}} Session in the programme](https://events.rdmobile.com/Lists/Details/2977203){.btn .btn-outline-secondary}

## Community ecology and evolution

### The other story told by urban ecology in the Global South {#idiv-urban}

*iDiv Seminar Series — German Centre for Integrative Biodiversity Research
(Halle-Jena-Leipzig), September 2024 · and Universität Bielefeld, 2025 · in
English*

Urban ecology written from the Global South rather than read from it: what
changes in the questions, in the study systems and in the conclusions when the
cities under study are Campo Grande and São José dos Campos instead of the
northern-hemisphere cities that dominate the literature. Given while a Humboldt
fellow on sabbatical at iDiv.

The slides below are the 2025 Bielefeld version of the talk.

[{{< fa solid file-pdf >}} Slides (PDF, 69 pp.)](talks/2024-idiv-urban-ecology-global-south.pdf){.btn .btn-outline-primary}

### Evolutionary macroecology of the Atlantic Forest of South America {#gottingen}

*16 May 2024 · [Biodiversity, Macroecology and Biogeography
group](https://www.uni-goettingen.de/en/128741.html), Faculty of Forest
Sciences and Forest Ecology, University of Göttingen · at the invitation of
Gustavo B. Paterno · in English*

The regional species pool of the Atlantic Forest as a macroevolutionary
product: how biogeographic history, diversification and the evolution of
ecologically relevant traits combine to shape the assemblages we sample today.
Given during a Humboldt-funded sabbatical at iDiv.

[{{< fa solid file-pdf >}} Slides (PDF, 26 pp.)](talks/2024-gottingen-evolutionary-macroecology.pdf){.btn .btn-outline-primary}

### Usos e desusos de métodos filogenéticos comparativos {#pcm-unesp}

*23 September 2016 · Seminários Gerais em Biodiversidade Aquática, Graduate
Programme in Aquatic Biodiversity — Instituto de Biociências do Câmpus do
Litoral Paulista, UNESP · at the invitation of Ivan Nunes · 2 h · in
Portuguese*

What phylogenetic comparative methods are for, what they are routinely asked
to do that they cannot, and how to tell the two apart — the main legitimate
uses, the common misuses, and practical advice for choosing a method.

The deck kept being revised after the seminar, so a few slides cite work
published later.

[{{< fa solid file-pdf >}} Slides (PDF, 56 pp.)](talks/2016-unesp-clp-metodos-filogeneticos-comparativos.pdf){.btn .btn-outline-primary}

### Eco-evolutionary dynamics in metacommunities {#eco-evo-metacom}

*1 September 2020 · II Workshop of Community Ecology, held online 31 August –
4 September 2020, organised by IBILCE/UNESP (São José do Rio Preto) and UFRPE
and coordinated by Denise de Cerqueira Rossa-Feres · in English; also given in
Portuguese at UEPB*

Why community ecology cannot simply set evolution aside: evolutionary change
can happen fast enough to alter ecological dynamics within the span of a study.
A recap of the population genetics needed, worked examples of processes feeding
back into one another, what eco-evolutionary dynamics are and — as importantly
— what they are not, and what it takes to let a metacommunity evolve.

[{{< fa solid file-pdf >}} Slides (PDF, 101 pp.)](talks/2020-ii-workshop-eco-evolutionary-dynamics.pdf){.btn .btn-outline-primary}
&nbsp;
[{{< fa brands youtube >}} Watch](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZRLomP-K0o4&list=PLy2rjqiD2VP4M8K-19Whs0bs3bHQEGvwJ){.btn .btn-outline-secondary}

*13 April 2017 · Science Club, Department of Biosciences, Swansea University,

How the anuran assemblages of the Brazilian Atlantic Forest came to be what

## Conference presentations

### The tempo and mode of body size evolution in charontid whip spiders {#evolution-whip-spiders}

*June 2026 · Macroevolution session, Evolution 2026 · in English*

With Paulo M. Martins, Gabriela A. Galvão, Thiago Gonçalves-Souza and Gustavo
S. de Miranda. Amblypygi emerged over 330 million years ago and kept a
remarkably conserved body plan — an evolutionary paradox next to the adaptive
radiations other lineages show on reaching new niches. The talk disentangles
the climatic from the habitat drivers of what body size variation there is.

Published as Martins et al. 2026, *Evolution*
([10.1093/evolut/qpag138](https://doi.org/10.1093/evolut/qpag138)).

[{{< fa solid file-pdf >}} Slides (PDF, 14 pp.)](talks/2026-evolution-whip-spiders.pdf){.btn .btn-outline-primary}

### The tempo and mode of tadpole body shape evolution {#asn-asilomar}

*9 January 2021 · American Society of Naturalists stand-alone meeting, Virtual
Asilomar · session "Contributed Papers II: Trait Evolution" · in English*

With Marcos Rafael Severgnini. Free-swimming tadpoles occupy habitats with very
different hydrodynamics — permanent and temporary ponds, streams, phytotelmata,
tree holes — and the larval morphospace shows repeated convergence. The talk
asks at what rate, and under which model, that body-shape variation accumulated.

[{{< fa solid file-pdf >}} Slides (PDF, 26 pp.)](talks/2021-asn-asilomar-tadpole-body-shape.pdf){.btn .btn-outline-primary}
&nbsp;
[{{< fa brands youtube >}} Watch (from 4:20:48)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zxIyjsI3VQw&t=15648s){.btn .btn-outline-secondary}
